parts.name: frame steel

physics.Basic_description: The main body of the wrench, painted white/light grey, consisting of a long cylindrical shaft and a bulky head frame with a rectangular opening.
physics.Functional_description: Provides the structural backbone and leverage arm for the tool, housing the adjustment mechanism and fixed jaw.
physics.Grasped_description: A gripper can firmly grasp the cylindrical shaft section to apply torque or lift the tool.
physics.reason: Pipe wrenches are typically made of heavy cast iron or steel; the shaft and frame are solid or thick-walled structural components designed for high torque.

parts.description: The main body of the wrench, painted white/light grey, consisting of a long cylindrical shaft and a bulky head frame with a rectangular opening.
parts.function: Provides the structural backbone and leverage arm for the tool, housing the adjustment mechanism and fixed jaw.

parts.name: ferrule

physics.Basic_description: A small grey metallic ring located between the wooden handle and the main shaft.
physics.Functional_description: Secures the wooden handle to the metal shaft and prevents splitting.
physics.Grasped_description: Too small and smooth to be a primary grasp point; likely slippery.
physics.reason: Small metal collar, effectively solid for mass estimation purposes.

parts.description: A small grey metallic ring located between the wooden handle and the main shaft.
parts.function: Secures the wooden handle to the metal shaft and prevents splitting.

parts.name: handle body

physics.Basic_description: A brown, cylindrical wooden handle with a smooth varnished finish, tapering slightly towards the end.
physics.Functional_description: Provides a comfortable grip for the user to apply force without slipping.
physics.Grasped_description: Ideal for a parallel jaw gripper to hold the tool securely due to its cylindrical shape and friction.
physics.reason: Tool handles are solid wood dowels or turned pieces.

parts.description: A brown, cylindrical wooden handle with a smooth varnished finish, tapering slightly towards the end.
parts.function: Provides a comfortable grip for the user to apply force without slipping.

parts.name: handle worn

physics.Basic_description: The very end of the wooden handle, appearing slightly lighter or worn in the segmentation.
physics.Functional_description: The terminal end of the grip, often used for hanging or pushing.
physics.Grasped_description: Too close to the edge to be a stable grasp point on its own.
physics.reason: Continuation of the solid wooden handle.

parts.description: The very end of the wooden handle, appearing slightly lighter or worn in the segmentation.
parts.function: The terminal end of the grip, often used for hanging or pushing.

parts.name: butt cap

physics.Basic_description: A small grey metallic cap at the very end of the wooden handle.
physics.Functional_description: Protects the end of the wooden handle from damage and wear.
physics.Grasped_description: Too small and rounded for a secure functional grasp.
physics.reason: Small metal end cap, treated as solid component.

parts.description: A small grey metallic cap at the very end of the wooden handle.
parts.function: Protects the end of the wooden handle from damage and wear.

parts.name: jaw steel

physics.Basic_description: A dark grey/purple metallic block with serrated teeth, sliding within the head frame.
physics.Functional_description: Clamps against the workpiece when the nut is adjusted, providing the gripping force.
physics.Grasped_description: Can be grasped to manually adjust position if the nut is loose, but primarily a functional interface.
physics.reason: Jaws must be solid forged steel to withstand crushing forces without deforming.

parts.description: A dark grey/purple metallic block with serrated teeth, sliding within the head frame.
parts.function: Clamps against the workpiece when the nut is adjusted, providing the gripping force.

parts.name: nut knurled

physics.Basic_description: A cyan-colored knurled wheel/nut located in the slot of the wrench head.
physics.Functional_description: Rotated by hand to move the movable jaw up or down to adjust the grip size.
physics.Grasped_description: Designed to be pinched and rotated by fingers or a fine gripper tip.
physics.reason: Knurled nuts are solid metal cylinders to transmit torque effectively.

simulation.collision: CoACD convex decomposition of concave source collision meshes (relative tolerance 0.03–0.05)
simulation.inertia: Source URDF link inertials; missing inertials use geometry-derived defaults (density 1000 kg/m³)
simulation.friction: Source URDF mu1 as sliding friction; torsional 0.005, rolling 0.0001
simulation.contact: MuJoCo soft contacts (solref 0.01 1); source restitution is displayed, not converted
simulation.material: Rigid bodies; Young’s modulus and Poisson ratio are annotations, not soft-body parameters

interaction.description: Switchable virtual joint damping and reflected armature for interactive inspection; source properties are unchanged.
interaction.rule: damping ≥ rated effort / rated speed; armature = 2% child subtree mass (slide) or 2% mass × collision radius² (hinge)

collisionFilter.description: Self-contact excluded between directly connected rigid groups, including the fixed base; nonadjacent contacts retained
